analysis.investment_thesis: A sub-scale commodity foundry earning 7.4% ROCE — below the cost of capital — trading at 25x earnings is the opposite of a Munger investment. Invert: this is precisely what we avoid — low returns, no moat, priced like a compounder.
key_strengths: Promoter holding of 70.88% signals skin-in-the-game alignment
Export-oriented castings business with 37+ years of operating history since 1988
Asset-backed manufacturing with tangible book value support
key_risks: ROCE of 7.41% and ROE of 6.20% destroy capital vs ~12% cost of equity in India
Castings & forgings is a commodity with no durable competitive advantage or pricing power
Tiny INR 66 Cr market cap = illiquidity, disclosure thinness, and governance risk
red_flags: P/E of 25.4x on 6.2% ROE implies ~4% earnings yield — priced like a quality compounder while earning commodity returns
Return on capital below cost of capital means growth actively destroys shareholder value
Cyclical metals exposure with customer concentration typical of small foundries
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Invert, always invert. What would make this a bad investment? A business earning 7.4% on capital in a commodity industry with no pricing power, trading at 25x earnings with a 66 Cr market cap. Super Iron ticks every box on that list. Castings & forgings is the kind of capital-hungry, cyclical, margin-thin business Buffett and I have spent decades learning to avoid — you pour capital in, the customer captures the surplus, and you end up with rust and receivables. ROE of 6.2% is below a bank FD; compounding at that rate is wealth destruction after inflation.

The 70.88% promoter holding is the only mildly positive signal, but alignment without ability produces nothing. At 25x earnings the market is already paying for a turnaround that the numbers don't support — I'd need to see ROCE above 15% sustained for 3–5 years before even opening the annual report seriously. Pass. There are better fish in the pond; stay in your circle of competence and wait for a great business at a fair price, not a mediocre one at a rich price.
